question: Does causal anterior/prefrontal intervention selectively affect confidence-based perceptual metacognition, and is that sufficient to infer phenomenal necessity?

sources.grade: E2 original main Methods/Results/Discussion, no raw or supplementary reanalysis
sources.positive: Selective impairment of perceptual confidence-versus-accuracy metacognition; memory metacognition comparatively preserved
sources.negative_limits: Anterior-PFC perceptual meta-d'/d' 95% CI 0.28-0.64 versus memory 0.78-1.29; small heterogeneous clinical groups; not phenomenal necessity
sources.counterhypotheses: Chronic network effects, selection, compensation, surgery causes, domain-specific metacognitive report only
sources.rights: Author 2014/Oxford University Press; exact reuse grant not verified, critical paraphrase only

sources.authors: Rounis, Maniscalco, Rothwell, Passingham and Lau
sources.grade: E1 original abstract plus later independent E2 source commentary; original full main not available in this run
sources.study_type: Sham-controlled bilateral DLPFC cTBS metacognitive visual report
sources.positive: Original authors report lower confidence/visibility metacognitive sensitivity with objective discrimination held stable
sources.negative_limits: 2017 independent comparison found 13/20 original participants had at least one unstable signal-detection block; no original raw rerun performed
sources.counterhypotheses: Boundary data instability, sham controls, contrast staircase and label wording, physiological target uncertainty
sources.rights: Taylor & Francis; no open redistribution license established

sources.grade: E2 entire accessible original PLOS main Methods/Results/Discussion, no raw reproduction
sources.study_type: Independent attempted partial replication and extension of Rounis cTBS
sources.positive: Active vertex controls, explicit robust signal-detection exclusions and cross-measure assessment
sources.negative_limits: No TMS x site effect in experiment1 meta-d'-d' F(4,48)=0.06 p>0.1; experiment2 3 decreases/4 increases among 7 putative responders, no replicable selective impairment; effect estimate +0.07 rather than -0.35
sources.counterhypotheses: Altered report label, 5cm heuristic coil target not verified physiological suppression, small final groups, contingent rather than fully crossed repeat sessions
sources.rights: CC BY 4.0 original PLOS main article; no data/figures/code copied
